children: SoftBank Group shares plunged 13.8% in Tokyo on Wednesday November 25, the steepest fall among Japan's major technology names, as investors grew nervous again about the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
The slump dragged Asian technology stocks lower and set the tone for a broad sell-off in chip-related companies across the region, showing how quickly confidence in AI-linked companies could turn.

SoftBank's slide did not happen in isolation. Other firms linked to the global AI supply chain suffered almost as much, according to market data on Wednesday. Advantest, which supplies chip-testing equipment to Nvidia, dropped 12.7%.

Tokyo Electron, which sells chipmaking equipment to Nvidia's manufacturing partner TSMC, lost 11.82%. Lasertec, a maker of chip inspection equipment, shed 10.15%, while Disco Corporation fell 9.41% and Renesas Electronics lost 9%.

The effect had even spread to South Korea, where Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each tumbled more than 7%. Both companies are key suppliers of high-bandwidth memory chips, a fast type of memory that AI accelerators need to process huge volumes of data. LG Innotek, another technology firm, lost 3.8%.

The losses followed a fall in US technology shares overnight. Wall Street's weakness fed straight into Asian trading. The Nasdaq Composite gave back some of the sharp gains it made in the previous session, when Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's chief executive.

Tech stocks had swung wildly for several months as investors had worried about how much companies spent on AI equipment, doubted whether that spending would pay off, and questioned circular financing, in which firms fund one another's AI deals. Huang's ouster as Nvidia chief executive added fresh worries for investors, and his return then sparked a massive rally.

By Wednesday's session, six Japanese technology and chip stocks had lost at least 9% each, while the two South Korean memory giants had shed more than 7% each. The moves reversed part of the optimism that Huang's return had created in the market a day earlier, and they extended the overnight decline in the Nasdaq Composite.

title: SoftBank shares crash 14% as Asian tech stocks fall on AI rally concerns
